data.title: Thousands protest in Turkey over journalists' arrests, media shutdowns
data.description: ISTANBUL - Thousands rallied in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday against what they described as growing pressure on journalists in Turkey, including arrests, media shutdowns and the appointment of state administrators.

data.title: Thousands gather at new Albanian anti-government rally
data.description: TIRANA (ALBANIA) - Thousands rallied in Tirana on Saturday at a fresh anti-government rally after days of violent unrest in the Albanian capital, with police firing tear gas to disperse the crowd.

data.title: French police fire tear gas during fresh protests
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French police fired tear gas on Saturday to prevent protesters in several cities from advancing to their centres, in fresh nationwide demonstrations held a week after riots broke out, AFP journalists saw.

data.title: Nigeria's Tinubu defends record as economy bites ahead of election
data.description: KADUNA (NIGERIA) - President Bola Tinubu kicked off his re-election campaign Saturday promising "a better tomorrow" as Nigeria prepares to head to the polls in a vote set to be defined by the rising cost of living.

data.title: Israeli forces displace Hebron families after deadly attack
data.description: HEBRON (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron on Saturday and displaced around 250 families, vowing to exact a heavy price for an attack the day before in which two Palestinians killed two soldiers before being gunned down.

data.title: France extends detention of suspected racist shooter
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Police found a copy of Adolf Hitler's "Mein Kampf" at the home of the man suspected of a gun attack in the Paris suburbs that killed one person and wounded five, a source close to the investigation told AFP Saturday.

data.title: Seen and heard at protests in France
data.description: PARIS - AFP has deployed reporters, photographers and video journalists in cities across France to document massive cost-of-living protests expected to take place nationwide on Saturday.

data.title: North Korean leader makes unannounced visit to Chinese border city
data.description: SEOUL - North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appears to have arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong, a government source in Seoul and South Korean media said on Saturday.

data.title: Thai foreign minister welcomes US-Myanmar engagement
data.description: LISBON - Thailand welcomes ​US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Asean summit next month in Manila on how to ‌proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said on Friday.

data.title: Security high as France braces for new protests
data.description: PARIS - France was erecting a ring of steel in major cities ahead of new protests Saturday, with police, helicopters and armoured vehicles seeking to prevent a repeat of the violence and looting which erupted during nationwide demonstrations last weekend.

data.title: Suspect arrested after fire at Hitler’s mountain retreat
data.description: BERLIN - German police said on Saturday they had detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler’s mountain retreat, known as the Eagle’s Nest, in the state of Bavaria.

data.title: Kim Jong Un calls for ‘Korean-style military revolution’
data.description: SEOUL - North Korean leader Kim Jong Un urged his military to train to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media said on Saturday.

data.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with CIA, but discreetly
data.description: WASHINGTON - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday called for Cubans to make “discreet” contact with the American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island’s communist government.

data.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with CIA, but warns: be discreet
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday called for Cubans to make "discreet" contact with the American intelligence services as Washington seeks to force an end to the island's communist government.

data.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
data.description: GENEVA (SWITZERLAND) - The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said.

data.title: Signs point to renewed major US military ops against Iran
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The United States appears to be preparing to resume large-scale strikes against Iran, but there is unlikely to be a military solution for either side in the devastating conflict, experts say.

data.title: Trump orders lawsuit to block Alaska Senate result if Republicans lose
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - President Donald Trump on Friday said he ordered a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to prevent certification of Alaska's Senate election result if the Republican incumbent loses -- ramping up questions over whether he will accept midterms defeat.

data.title: Melania Trump says she brokered truce in war-torn Ukrainian city
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US First Lady Melania Trump said in a surprise announcement Friday she had brokered a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged city of Oleshky, where citizens are trapped and running out of food.

data.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
data.description: NAIROBI - A multi-storey building under construction collapsed in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site.

data.title: Meghan ‘distressed’ by reports father had child-abuse images
data.description: LONDON - Prince Harry’s wife Meghan said on Friday she was “deeply distressed” by accusations that her father had images of child abuse, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations.

data.title: Gunman kills one, wounds four in town outside Paris
data.description: TRAPPES, France - A gunman firing from his car killed one person and wounded four in the Paris suburb of Trappes on Friday, authorities said, with at least two victims from immigrant backgrounds and prosecutors investigating the case as a potential “terrorist” act.

data.title: Tanker with Russian diesel heads to New York
data.description: A tanker filled with Russian diesel is headed for New York, maritime trackers and the Kremlin confirmed on Friday, after the United States eased sanctions in a deal that shocked Ukraine and its European allies.

data.title: Romania blames Russia for deadly attack on ship
data.description: BUCHAREST - Romania said on Friday one sailor had died and three were missing after a ship was struck by a drone and sank in the latest attack in the Black Sea that President Nicusor Dan blamed on Russia.

data.title: ‘Fake’ pollsters exposed before US elections
data.description: WASHINGTON — A polling firm whose data was tracked by political campaigns and mainstream media has admitted that its polls were fabricated, in the second such scandal to stir controversy ahead of the midterm elections.

data.title: Israel-linked navigation app hits back at Malaysian claims
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - The navigation app Waze has rejected Malaysia’s allegations that it could exploit users’ personal data, after the country banned civil servants from using the app over its Israeli links.

data.title: Ukraine holds teen girl in Russian poison plot targeting soldiers
data.description: KYIV - Ukrainian police said on Friday that they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

data.title: Greece bans social media for under-15s
data.description: ATHENS - Greece's parliament passed a law on Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people's use of the apps.

data.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
data.description: PARIS - France is bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

data.title: Speculation abounds on Trump-Kim meeting ahead of Apec summit
data.description: SEOUL - As world leaders prepare to gather in Shenzhen for November's Apec summit, speculation is mounting over a possible meeting between Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un—a prospect experts say remains remote.

data.title: How five Boeing 777s linked Madagascar’s power elite to Iran
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - Once among Madagascar’s most influential businessmen and a close ally of deposed president Andry Rajoelina, Mamy Ravatomanga stands at the centre of one of the island’s most explosive corruption cases.
